classes.name: Unguarded concurrent access to shared state
classes.definition: Two or more concurrent operations read a shared value, decide based on it, and write back, without any mechanism guaranteeing the value did not change in between.
prose_signals: two users at the same time
classes.code_pattern: A read of shared state (db row, cache entry, in-memory counter), followed by a conditional, followed by a write to that same state, with an await or IO boundary in between and no transaction, lock, or atomic operation.
classes.guardrail_strategy: Require that any read-decide-write sequence on shared state is performed inside a transaction, an atomic database operation, or behind an explicit lock. Reject the pattern where an availability check and the corresponding claim are separate statements.
classes.test_strategy: Fire N concurrent requests at the same endpoint with Promise.all and assert the invariant holds exactly once.
classes.notes: Highest value class for the demo. The failure is invisible in single-threaded manual testing, which is exactly why it survives code review.

classes.name: External input reaches a sink without validation
classes.definition: A value originating outside the system boundary (request body, query string, header, webhook payload, third-party response) is used in a query, filesystem path, computation, or downstream call without being validated or constrained first.
prose_signals: crashed when the field was missing
classes.code_pattern: Direct destructuring or property access on req.body / req.query / req.params followed by use in a query, arithmetic, or an outbound call, with no schema validation, type check, or bounds check on the path between.
classes.guardrail_strategy: Require every route handler to validate its inputs against an explicit schema before any business logic runs. Reject direct use of req.* values below the first validation boundary.
classes.test_strategy: Send the malformed payload from the incident and assert a 4xx with a useful message, not a 5xx or a silent success.
classes.notes: Easiest class to detect and to write a rule for. Good safety net if other classes prove hard.

classes.name: Operation with no upper bound
classes.definition: A query, loop, allocation, or fan-out whose size is determined by data rather than by an explicit limit, so it grows without bound as the dataset grows.
classes.code_pattern: A collection-returning query with no limit, skip, or pagination; or an await inside a loop over an unbounded collection; or an unbounded Promise.all fan-out.
classes.guardrail_strategy: Require an explicit limit on every collection query and every fan-out. A default page size must be applied when the caller does not supply one.
classes.test_strategy: Seed a large fixture, call the endpoint, assert the returned collection size is capped and the response time stays under a threshold.
classes.notes: The rule is prone to false positives on legitimately small collections. Expect this class to land in needs_review sometimes, which is fine and honest.

classes.name: Edge of the valid range handled incorrectly
classes.definition: The code is correct for typical values but wrong at a boundary: empty collection, single element, zero, negative, maximum, first or last item, midnight, month end, or a rounding edge.
prose_signals: only when there was exactly one
classes.code_pattern: Indexing with length arithmetic, slicing without an emptiness check, date arithmetic on raw components, or float arithmetic on money.
classes.guardrail_strategy: Require an explicit empty and single-element branch wherever a collection is indexed, and require money and dates to go through the designated helper rather than raw arithmetic.
classes.test_strategy: Parameterised test over the boundary set: empty, one, two, max, and the specific value from the incident.
classes.notes: Very common in real postmortems and easy to write convincing incident reports for.

classes.name: Acquired resource not released on every path
classes.definition: A connection, file handle, lock, timer, subscription, or listener is acquired but released only on the success path, so failures leak it.
classes.code_pattern: An acquire call whose matching release is not inside a finally block, or is absent on an early return or throw path.
classes.guardrail_strategy: Require every acquire to be paired with a release in a finally block, or to use a scoped helper that guarantees release.
classes.test_strategy: Force the failure path repeatedly and assert the resource counter returns to baseline.
classes.notes: The 'fixed by a restart' signal in prose is a very strong tell and makes for a readable incident report.

classes.name: Failure caught and treated as success
classes.definition: An error is caught and then ignored, logged only, or converted into a benign-looking value, so the caller proceeds as if the operation succeeded.
prose_signals: we did not notice for days
classes.code_pattern: A catch block with an empty body, a bare console.log, or a return of null, empty array, or a default value that is indistinguishable from a legitimate result.
classes.guardrail_strategy: Forbid catch blocks that neither rethrow, nor return a typed failure, nor emit a structured error event. A catch must make the failure visible to someone.
classes.test_strategy: Force the underlying operation to fail and assert the caller observes a failure rather than an empty success.
classes.notes: Detection is unusually reliable because the anti-pattern is syntactic. Good class to include if time allows.

classes.name: Caller and callee disagree on the shape
classes.definition: Two components hold different assumptions about a payload, response, or config shape, and nothing enforces the agreement, so a change on one side breaks the other silently.
classes.code_pattern: Deep property access on an external response without a guard, or a hand-written object literal duplicating a shape defined elsewhere.
classes.guardrail_strategy: Require external responses to be parsed through a declared schema at the boundary, and forbid duplicating a shape that already has a canonical definition.
classes.test_strategy: Feed a response missing the field and assert a clear boundary error rather than a downstream crash.
classes.notes: Hardest class to detect statically. Include only if the core five are done and working.
